easy.prompt: What is the length (Euclidean norm) of the vector (3, 4) in ℝ²?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's the squared norm 3² + 4²; take the square root for the length.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That's 3 + 4, not the Pythagorean combination of components.

easy.prompt: Compute the dot product (1, 2) · (3, 4).
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's 1 + 2 + 3 + 4, not componentwise multiplication summed.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Off by one in the arithmetic.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's 2·7 or another product — use (1)(3) + (2)(4).

easy.prompt: In ℝ³, the standard basis vector e₂ is…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: e₂ has a 1 in the second coordinate and 0 elsewhere.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's e₁, not e₂.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Not a standard basis vector.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's e₃.

easy.prompt: What is the 2 × 2 identity matrix I₂?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: I₂ has ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere; it leaves vectors unchanged under multiplication.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That matrix is singular and does not preserve all vectors.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That swaps coordinates — it's a permutation matrix, not the identity.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Rows are dependent; not the identity.

easy.prompt: A matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns is described as…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: By convention, m × n means m rows and n columns.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: A 2 × 2 matrix has only two columns.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That requires three rows and three columns.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That would be 3 rows and 2 columns — dimensions are reversed.

easy.prompt: In row echelon form, the leading entry of each nonzero row (the pivot) lies…

choices.label: B
choices.body: Below the pivot in the same column

choices.label: C
choices.body: Strictly to the right of the pivot in the row above.

choices.label: D
choices.body: In the same column as every other pivot

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Echelon form forces pivots to move right as you go down the rows.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Pivots appear across columns depending on the matrix.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That would be a zero below each pivot in REF, not the definition of pivot position.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Pivots generally shift right; they need not share a column.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's ad + bc or a sign error — use ad − bc.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's 1 + 2 + 3 + 4, not a determinant.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Wrong combination of products.

easy.prompt: A scalar λ is an eigenvalue of A if there exists a nonzero vector v with…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Eigenvalues are defined through nontrivial solutions to (A − λI)v = 0.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That would mean A is the zero matrix on all inputs, not an eigenpair.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That would mean every vector is an eigenvector with the same λ — far stronger than one eigenpair.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: det A is a single number for the matrix, not the eigenvalue condition.

easy.prompt: The vectors (1, 2) and (2, 4) in ℝ² are…

choices.label: B
choices.body: Linearly dependent (one is a scalar multiple of the other).

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: (2, 4) = 2(1, 2), so one lies in the span of the other.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Their dot product is 1·2 + 2·4 = 10 ≠ 0.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: A nontrivial combination 2·(1,2) − 1·(2,4) = 0 shows dependence.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: They live in ℝ² and there are only two vectors anyway.

easy.prompt: The span of a single nonzero vector v in ℝⁿ is…

choices.label: A
choices.body: All scalar multiples of v (a line through the origin).

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Span{v} = {cv : c ∈ ℝ}, a one-dimensional subspace when v ≠ 0.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: cv includes v itself when c = 1.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Scalar multiples need not have length 1.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: One nonzero vector cannot reach every direction in ℝⁿ unless n = 1.

easy.prompt: Two vectors u and v are orthogonal when…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Orthogonality in Euclidean space is defined by zero inner product.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: The cross product is a 3D tool; in ℝ² use the dot product.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Equal length does not imply perpendicularity.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Identical nonzero vectors are parallel, not orthogonal.

easy.prompt: When Ax = b has no exact solution (overdetermined inconsistent system), least squares seeks x that…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Least squares minimizes the residual norm, giving the best fit in the column space of A.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: If no exact solution exists, that goal is impossible.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: x = 0 is optimal only in special cases.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That would be the worst fit, not the best.

easy.prompt: If u = (1, −1) and v = (2, 3), then u + v equals…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's v − u.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Mixed components from multiplication, not addition.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's u − v or a sign error on the second component.

easy.prompt: If A is 2 × 3 and B is 3 × 4, the product AB has size…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Inner dimensions must match (3); the result has the outer dimensions 2 × 4.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's the size of B, not the product.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's the size of A, not the product.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's only when both factors are 3 × 3.

easy.prompt: An augmented matrix [A | b] represents the linear system…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Columns of A combine with entries of x to produce b.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Variables are usually written as a column on the right of A.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Matrix sizes would not align for ordinary matrix-vector multiplication.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not the standard form of a linear system.

easy.prompt: For any n, det(Iₙ) equals…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: The identity matrix is invertible with determinant product of diagonal ones.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Determinant −1 arises from an odd number of row swaps of Iₙ, not Iₙ itself.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's the trace for Iₙ, not the determinant.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: A singular matrix has determinant zero; Iₙ is nonsingular.

easy.prompt: If Av = 3v for nonzero v, then 3 is…

choices.label: C
choices.body: An eigenvalue of A with eigenvector v

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: The equation matches Av = λv with λ = 3.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: det A equals the product of eigenvalues (with multiplicity) only in specific cases, not from one eigenpair alone.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: It is the eigenvalue in the defining equation.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: A may have other eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

easy.prompt: Any three vectors in ℝ² are…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: dim ℝ² = 2, so more than two vectors must satisfy a nontrivial dependence relation.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Dependence does not force orthogonality.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: A basis of ℝ² has exactly two independent vectors.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Impossible when count exceeds dimension.

easy.prompt: The standard basis {e₁, …, eₙ} spans…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Every vector is a linear combination of basis vectors with coefficients its entries.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: e₂, …, eₙ are needed for other coordinates.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Negative coefficients allow negative entries in combinations.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Each eᵢ is in the span, so the span is nonempty.

easy.prompt: The projection of (4, 0) onto the x-axis in ℝ² is…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: The vector already lies on the x-axis, so projection leaves it unchanged.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Only the zero vector projects to zero here; (4,0) is nonzero on the axis.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That's alignment with the y-axis, not the x-axis.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not collinear with the x-axis.

medium.prompt: Find a unit vector in the direction of v = (3, −4).
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That has length 5, not 1.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Opposite direction — still parallel but wrong sign if matching v's direction.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Swaps and signs — not parallel to (3, −4).

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Missed the contribution of the second column to the first row.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Second row should be 6, not 3.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: First-row arithmetic used 1+2 instead of 1·1 + 2·2.

medium.prompt: How many free variables can a 3 × 5 coefficient matrix have at most?
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: With 5 unknowns, free variables = 5 − rank; rank can be as low as 0, giving up to 5 free variables.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's the minimum free count when rank is 3, not the maximum.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Zero free variables require rank 5, impossible with only 3 rows unless the matrix is degenerate in a different sense.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's the maximum rank (row count), not the maximum free variables.

medium.prompt: If A is 3 × 3 with det A = 2, then det(2A) equals…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Scaling a 3 × 3 matrix by 2 multiplies the determinant by 2³ = 8; 8 · 2 = 16.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Added 2 to det A instead of multiplying by 2³.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Used factor 2 once instead of 2³.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Used 2² instead of 2³.

medium.prompt: The eigenvalues of [[2, 0], [0, 3]] are…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Diagonal matrices have eigenvalues on the diagonal.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Confused trace/determinant with individual eigenvalues.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Not the diagonal entries.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: The second eigenvalue is 3, not 0.

medium.prompt: Which set is linearly independent in ℝ³?
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: The standard basis has no nontrivial combination giving zero.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Second vector is 2 times the first — dependent.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: (1,1,0) and (2,2,0) are multiples — dependent triple.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Third vector is the sum of the first two — dependent.

medium.prompt: The span of {(1,0), (0,1)} in ℝ² is…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: The two vectors are the standard basis for ℝ².

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Contains (1,0) and (0,1).
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That line is span{(1,1)}, not the coordinate axes.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: (0,1) is not on the x-axis but is in the span.

medium.prompt: Apply Gram–Schmidt to v₁ = (1, 0) and v₂ = (1, 1). The orthogonal second vector is…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's v₁, not the component perpendicular to v₁.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: v₂ is not parallel to v₁, so the perpendicular part is nonzero.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not orthogonal to v₁ — dot product is 1.

medium.prompt: The normal equations for least squares with full column rank A are…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Minimizing ‖Ax − b‖² leads to AᵀAx = Aᵀb when AᵀA is invertible.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Missing transpose on the first factor — wrong derivation.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Used when an exact solution exists, not the least-squares substitute.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: A may not be square or invertible.

medium.prompt: The angle between u = (1, 0) and v = (1, 1) satisfies cos θ = …
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Would mean orthogonal vectors.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Would correspond to θ = 60° in a different configuration.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Cosine cannot exceed 1.

medium.prompt: Which matrix is invertible?
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: det [[1,2],[3,7]] = 7 − 6 = 1 ≠ 0; the others have dependent rows.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Row 2 is 2× row 1 — determinant zero.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Identical rows — singular.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Zero row — singular.

medium.prompt: A homogeneous system Ax = 0 with more unknowns than equations (n > m) always has…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Rank ≤ m < n, so there are free variables and infinitely many solutions including x ≠ 0.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Free variables prevent uniqueness when n > rank.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: x = 0 is always a solution for homogeneous systems.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: A need not be square.

medium.prompt: If A and B are 2 × 2, then det(AB) equals…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Determinant is multiplicative: det(AB) = det A det B.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not the product rule.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Determinant is not additive in general.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: det(A + B) rarely equals det A det B.

medium.prompt: The characteristic polynomial of A = [[0, 1], [1, 0]] is…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: det([[−λ, 1], [1, −λ]]) = λ² − 1; eigenvalues ±1.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Missed the 1 from off-diagonal.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Degree 1 — characteristic polynomial is degree 2 for 2 × 2.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Sign error on the diagonal product.

medium.prompt: A set containing the zero vector is always…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: 1·0 + 0·(other vectors) = 0 is a nontrivial dependence on the zero vector alone.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: The zero vector alone gives a nontrivial combination.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Bases consist of independent vectors; zero cannot be in a basis.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Independence fails before discussing normalization.

medium.prompt: If S = {(1,0,0), (0,1,0)}, then dim(span S) equals…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: The two vectors are independent and lie in a plane in ℝ³.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: They are not parallel.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Span contains nonzero vectors.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Two non-coplanar-independent vectors in ℝ³ span a plane, not all of ℝ³.

medium.prompt: If Q is an orthogonal matrix, then QᵀQ equals…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Orthogonal means Qᵀ = Q⁻¹, so QᵀQ = I.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Would imply Qᵀ = I, not generally true.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Orthogonal matrices are invertible.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not the defining identity.

medium.prompt: Fitting a line y = a + bx to data points minimizes…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Ordinary least squares penalizes (yᵢ − a − bxᵢ)².

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That describes minimax (Chebyshev) fit, not least squares.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: xᵢ are fixed inputs, not residuals.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Independent variable error is not the standard least-squares objective.

medium.prompt: The cross product (0, 0, 1) × (0, 1, 0) in ℝ³ equals…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Standard right-hand rule: i × j = k, so k × j = −i.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not orthogonal to (0,1,0).
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Result must be perpendicular to both factors — not along z.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Sign reversed from k × j.

medium.prompt: The transpose of [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]] is…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Transpose swaps rows and columns: 2 × 3 becomes 3 × 2.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's a 180° reversal, not transpose.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Wrong dimensions and entries.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Only symmetric matrices equal their transpose.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Row 2 equals 2× row 1; eliminating leaves two pivot rows — rank 2.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Rows 1 and 3 are not multiples of each other.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Matrix is nonzero.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Row 2 is dependent, so there cannot be three independent rows.

hard.prompt: If A is 4 × 4 with det A = 5, then det(A⁻¹) equals…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: det(A⁻¹) = 1/det A = 1/5.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Would be (det A)⁻⁴, not the correct exponent.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That's det A, not det(A⁻¹).
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Determinant of inverse is reciprocal, not negated.

hard.prompt: A 2 × 2 matrix with trace 5 and determinant 6 has eigenvalues…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Eigenvalues solve λ² − (tr)λ + det = λ² − 5λ + 6 = (λ−2)(λ−3).

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Sum 5 but product 4, not 6.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Product would be 6 but sum would be −5, not 5.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Confused trace and determinant with eigenvalues.

hard.prompt: The dimension of the space of 2 × 2 symmetric matrices is…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Symmetric 2 × 2 matrices depend on three parameters: two diagonal entries and one off-diagonal (equal top-right and bottom-left).

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: More than one independent symmetric matrix exists.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Too few — diagonal and off-diagonal constraints need three degrees of freedom.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's all 2 × 2 matrices without symmetry.

hard.prompt: The column space of a 3 × 2 matrix A with rank 2 in ℝ³ is…

choices.label: C
choices.body: A line through the origin only

choices.label: D
choices.body: A plane through the origin (2-dimensional subspace)

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Rank 2 with two columns means the two columns are independent and span a 2D subspace.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Column space always contains 0 and column vectors.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Would require rank 3.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Would require rank 1.

hard.prompt: If W is a subspace of ℝⁿ, then (W⊥)⊥ equals…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: In finite-dimensional inner product spaces, double orthogonal complement returns W.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Only true when W = {0} or W = ℝⁿ in special cases.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: One complement is not the double complement.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Only when W = ℝⁿ.

hard.prompt: If the columns of A are orthonormal, the least-squares solution to Ax ≈ b is…

choices.label: C
choices.body: x = (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀb only when A is not orthonormal

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: With orthonormal columns, AᵀA = I and the normal equations reduce to x = Aᵀb.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: b need not lie in the column space.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That formula always holds; it simplifies to Aᵀb when columns are orthonormal.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: A is typically rectangular — no ordinary inverse.

hard.prompt: Let u, v be nonzero. ‖u + v‖ = ‖u‖ + ‖v‖ holds if and only if…

choices.label: A
choices.body: u and v are nonnegative scalar multiples in the same direction

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Triangle inequality is equality exactly when vectors are parallel and point the same way.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Then u + v = 0, not full norm additivity of positive lengths in the same direction sense.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Orthogonal nonzero vectors give strict inequality.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Triangle inequality is usually strict.

hard.prompt: If A is m × n with rank r, how many pivot columns appear in any echelon form of A?
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Pivot count equals rank — dimension of column space.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Column count can exceed rank when columns are dependent.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not a standard invariant.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Row count upper-bounds rank but pivots equal rank, not always m.

hard.prompt: The solution set of Ax = b with a particular solution xₚ and homogeneous solutions xₕ is…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Affine line/plane/hyperplane: translate the null space by any particular solution.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Homogeneous solutions can be added when the null space is nontrivial.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Misses the particular solution shift unless b = 0.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Consistent inhomogeneous systems have solutions.

hard.prompt: Swapping two rows of A multiplies det A by…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: A single row interchange flips the sign of the determinant.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Scaling rows by 2 affects det differently from swapping.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Swapping rows does not zero the determinant unless it was already zero for other reasons.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Would mean determinant unchanged — false for one swap.

hard.prompt: A matrix A with Aᵀ = −A (real skew-symmetric, n odd) must have eigenvalue 0 because…

choices.label: C
choices.body: Trace equals sum of squares of entries

choices.label: D
choices.body: det A = (−1)ⁿ det A forces det A = 0 when n is odd

hard.explanation: For odd n, det A = −det A implies det A = 0, so 0 is an eigenvalue.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Skew-symmetric eigenvalues are purely imaginary (zero real part).
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Skew-symmetric matrices are usually not diagonal.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Trace is zero for skew-symmetric A.

hard.prompt: If {v₁, v₂, v₃} is a basis of ℝ³ and T: ℝ³ → ℝ³ is linear with T(vᵢ) = eᵢ (standard basis), then T is…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Mapping a basis to a basis extends to an invertible linear transformation.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Rank 3 — spans all of ℝ³.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Given by linear extension from basis images.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Sends basis vectors to eᵢ, not to 0.

hard.prompt: The null space of [[1, 1, 0], [2, 2, 0]] is all vectors of the form…

choices.label: D
choices.body: all of ℝ³ with no restriction

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: x₁ + x₂ = 0 gives x₂ = −x₁; x₃ is free — two-parameter family.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Free variables yield infinitely many solutions.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Violates x₁ + x₂ = 0 unless t = 0.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Equation x₁ + x₂ = 0 restricts the first two coordinates.

hard.prompt: The matrix of the orthogonal projection onto the line spanned by unit vector u is…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: P = u(uᵀ) for unit u; (uᵀx)u = (uuᵀ)x.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's projection onto the orthogonal complement.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Missing transpose — wrong dimensions for ℝⁿ.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That's the scalar 1 for unit u, not the projection matrix.

hard.prompt: Multicollinearity (nearly dependent columns of A) in least squares mainly harms…

choices.label: A
choices.body: The fact that residuals are perpendicular to Col(A)

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: AᵀA becomes ill-conditioned; small data changes swing coefficients even though a minimizer exists.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Geometry of the residual stays; coefficient estimates become unstable.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: A least-squares minimizer still exists.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: The model remains linear in parameters.

hard.prompt: The reflection of vector x across the line spanned by unit u is…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Reflect = 2·proj_u x − x = 2uuᵀx − x.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Not the standard reflection formula.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's reflection across the orthogonal complement hyperplane.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That's projection onto u, not reflection.

hard.prompt: If A has singular value decomposition A = UΣVᵀ with Σ diagonal nonnegative, then ‖A‖₂ (operator 2-norm) equals…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: The spectral norm equals the top singular value.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's related to the smallest stretch, not the maximum.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Only defined for square A and not the operator norm.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Not the maximum stretch factor.

hard.prompt: For inconsistent system [A|b], a least-squares solution minimizes ‖Ax − b‖. Geometrically, Ax is the orthogonal projection of b onto…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: The closest point in the column space is the orthogonal projection of b.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Row space lives in domain space ℝⁿ, not target space where b lies.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Too large unless A is square and invertible — generally b's closest point is in Col(A) ⊂ ℝᵐ.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Null space contains only vectors mapped to 0, not approximations to b.

hard.prompt: An n × n matrix A is singular if and only if…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Invertibility and nonzero determinant are equivalent for square matrices.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Trace zero does not imply singularity.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Sufficient for singularity but not equivalent — singular matrices may have no zero row.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Many nonsymmetric matrices are invertible.
